agentCan: Implement the Auth Code with PKCE flow and the daily background refresh job RingCentral recommends
Implement the JWT-for-public-apps onboarding variant where a customer prefers it

approval.cost: No fee for creating an app, requesting scope approval, or App Gallery submission is stated in the guide
approval.trigger: Not for a standard public app using ordinary permissions, with three qualifications. (1) The old sandbox 'graduation' process is RETIRED: 'So, on March 14, 2024, we retired the application graduation process... Newly created applications began receiving credentials that work in both sandbox and production' (official announcement; the current Developer Guide contains no graduation requirement, and RingCentral's Embeddable docs confirm: 'Currently, new created RingCentral app will go to production directly'). Older material describing graduation criteria (exercise every permission, 5+ successful calls, error rate under 5%, manual SMS review) is obsolete. (2) Sensitive scopes ARE a live review gate: 'Some app scopes may include the text requires approval. These app scopes require approval because they will allow your application to perform sensitive operations. You are free to add these scopes to your app, and if you do, you will be required to provide an explanation and justification as to why your app requires the request functionality. Then, when you register your application, a support ticket will be filed automatically with the developer support team so that they can review and process your request.' More broadly, 'Public apps are subjected to greater scrutiny through the development process to ensure that RingCentral customers and their data are kept safe and secure.' (3) App Gallery listing is a separate, optional editorial submission (dedicated submission guide and final checklist; editorial feedback on copy quality and customer relevance); listing is NOT required for external users to connect. Separately, sending SMS triggers the TCR process (A2P 10DLC brand/campaign registration), a regulatory compliance gate rather than an OAuth review. No pre-approval caps are stated for standard public apps under the current model.
approval.wait: Not stated (no duration for scope-approval tickets or App Gallery review in the current Developer Guide)

blockers.detail: 'You cannot edit Application Type after your app has been created.' Public is required if users outside your own account will connect ('If your app is public then any RingCentral credential can be used to login to your application... If your app is private then only credentials belonging to your account can be used'). Pick Private by mistake and no external customer can ever log in; you must create a new app (new Client ID/secret, new redirect registrations).
blockers.howToClear: Choose Public deliberately at creation for any third-party SaaS use.
blockers.title: Application Type is a one-way door

blockers.detail: In the authorize request the scope parameter is 'Ignored... deferring to the permissions set by the developer when the app was created'. The token's scope is whatever permissions were configured on the app. Changing permissions means editing the app, not the request, and adding a 'requires approval' scope triggers the justification + support-ticket review even mid-lifecycle.
blockers.howToClear: Set the full permission set on the app up front; treat permission changes as releases, not requests.
blockers.title: Scopes are not requested at authorize time

blockers.detail: Refresh tokens are not issued unless enabled in app settings. They are single-use and rotate; refreshing immediately invalidates the previous access token ('there can only be one active access token at a time for user and app'), so two processes refreshing the same user's tokens break each other outside a ~10-second grace window (if the new access token is never used, the old refresh token 'remains valid for up to 60 minutes'). And 'You can only use a refresh token to refresh an access token that has not expired': refresh proactively before expiry.
blockers.howToClear: Enable refresh tokens at creation, run one serialized daily refresh job per connection, and always refresh before the access token expires.
blockers.title: Refresh tokens are opt-in and fragile

sources.label: Choosing the best auth method for your app (PKCE recommendation; JWT positioning)
Authorization code flow with PKCE (TTL parameters; refresh defaults)
Registering an application and obtaining app credentials (Public/Private; requires-approval scopes; password deprecation)
Using refresh tokens (single-use rotation; immediate access-token invalidation; grace windows)
Announcement: graduation retired March 14, 2024 (official RingCentral community; flagged, see Tested note)

tested: Read-only verification: app types, the PKCE and JWT flows, refresh semantics, and the scope-approval gate were checked against developers.ringcentral.com guide pages (some read via indexed excerpts of those same pages after one direct fetch was rate-limited) plus RingCentral's official developer FAQ. The graduation-retirement fact is cited from RingCentral's official community announcement because the Developer Guide itself no longer mentions graduation at all; RingCentral's official Embeddable docs corroborate that new apps go to production directly. A premise in the original research brief (that the JWT flow is being superseded) was checked and NOT confirmed: the guide deprecates only the password-based flow. No app created, nothing submitted.
unverified: Authorization code lifetime as a rule (no definitive numeric TTL is stated in the guide text read; only that the code 'expires quickly', that expires_in is returned with it, and an example showing expires_in=60).
The access-token TTL inconsistency (stated default 3600 seconds vs official sample responses showing expires_in 7199; the docs read do not explain the difference).

Review duration for 'requires approval' scope tickets and for App Gallery submission review (a 2020-era community answer cited 'up to 5 business days' for the retired manual SMS graduation review; that process no longer exists and the figure does not appear in current documentation).
Fees: no cost or fee for developer accounts, app creation, scope approval, or App Gallery listing is stated anywhere in the documentation read.
Pre-production usage caps for public apps under the current (post-graduation) model, and any numeric thresholds for the 'app quality monitoring program' referenced in the retirement announcement.

alternatives: JWT auth flow (RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant): for server apps with no user interface acting for a pre-determined user; a JWT credential generated by a user in the Developer Console (optionally restricted to specific apps by Client ID) is exchanged at the token endpoint. JWT credentials 'do not expire (unless you elect otherwise)', are 'persistent and cannot be changed once generated', and 'can be easily revoked by the owner or administrator'. RingCentral is explicit: 'JWT flow is NOT recommended for individual user authentication... JWT is ideally suited to authenticate a single service user (typically an admin)'. A JWT-for-public-apps pattern is also documented: each customer generates a JWT restricted to your app's Client ID and hands it over (the sanctioned replacement for asking for username/password)
Password-based (ROPC) flow: DEPRECATED. 'The password grant type has been deprecated. Developers should use the JWT auth flow as a superior and more secure alternative to password based auth.'
flavor.recommended: A Public, Server/Web REST API app using the 3-legged Authorization Code flow with PKCE, with refresh tokens enabled
flavor.why: The object is an 'app' created in the RingCentral Developer Console (Console > Apps > Create App); the primary category for API integrations is a 'REST API App', yielding a Client ID and Client Secret against sandbox (platform.devtest.ringcentral.com) and production (platform.ringcentral.com) base URLs. Two creation-time decisions define it: Application Type (Public vs Private: whose credentials may log in) and Platform Type (Server/Web for web apps, webhooks, and connecting another user's account). The official 'Choosing the best auth method' guide states: 'If your app's users need to independently log into RingCentral, the best authorization method is the Auth Code with PKCE Flow. However, some apps may elect to use the simpler, older, and less secure Auth Code Flow.'

humanMust: Create a RingCentral/developer account and the app in the Developer Console
Choose Application Type = Public (irreversible) and Platform Type = Server/Web
Register the OAuth redirect URI (exact match) and record the Client ID and Client Secret per environment
Decide on refresh tokens in the app's auth settings (not issued by default)
Select the app permissions under Security; if any is marked 'requires approval', supply the written explanation/justification (a support ticket is filed automatically)
name: RingCentral
nuances: Token endpoint throttling: the /token endpoint is limited to 5 requests per minute per application (per RingCentral's announcement); exceeding it yields HTTP 429 and 'continued violations may result in temporary suspension of the application'. Best practice: request a token once, cache it, reuse until expiry. Token-per-API-call designs will be throttled.

JWT credentials are immutable and user-bound: a JWT 'cannot be changed once generated' (only revoked and re-created) and represents exactly one user/extension, restrictable to specific app Client IDs. For public apps, each customer must manually generate a JWT in their own Developer Console and hand it over, a high-friction onboarding step compared with the 3-legged consent flow. RingCentral's migration guidance for moving an app from password to JWT auth warns the change is irreversible and recommends registering a second app to test first.

Environment split: sandbox and production use different base URLs AND different app credentials; sandbox test users/credentials are provided per app in the console. Exact-match redirect URIs apply to both the authorize and token calls.

An implicit-style pattern exists for stateless/single-page apps (the docs discuss passing refresh_token_ttl=0 for such apps), but PKCE is the documented recommendation for client-side apps. TTL parameters access_token_ttl / refresh_token_ttl can be passed at token time, but 'If the value specified exceeds the default one, the default value is applied' for refresh tokens.
prerequisites: The Application Type decision made before creation (Public for third-party use)
Refresh tokens enabled in the app's auth settings if durable connections are needed

steps.detail: Console > Apps > Create App > 'REST API App'. Choose Application Type = Public (required if users outside your own account will connect; cannot be edited later) and Platform Type = Server/Web. Declare whether you intend to promote the app in the App Gallery (the answer is 'for internal-use only').
steps.title: Create the app (Public, Server/Web)

steps.detail: Select '3-legged OAuth flow authorization code' (+ PKCE) and register the OAuth redirect URI (the value sent in the authorize request 'must exactly match one of the URIs you provided when creating your app'). In the auth settings, enable refresh tokens if users should 'authenticate once to your platform, and not be asked to login again'. Select permissions under Security (e.g. ReadAccounts, ReadCallLog, SMS); permissions are fixed at the app level. Record the Client ID and Client Secret (separate credentials per environment).
steps.title: Configure auth (PKCE, redirect URI, refresh tokens, permissions)

steps.detail: Generate code_verifier/code_challenge (S256 preferred; plain permitted). Redirect the user to platform.ringcentral.com/restapi/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256. The user logs in and authorizes.
steps.title: Redirect the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST /restapi/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, redirect_uri, code_verifier (the PKCE variant requires no client-secret Authorization header), optionally access_token_ttl / refresh_token_ttl. Store access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_token_expires_in, scope, and owner_id (extension ID). Access tokens default to 3600 seconds; refresh tokens to 7 days.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: RingCentral recommends 'a recurring background task that will wake up at least once per day, iterate over all access tokens stored locally, and exchange their refresh token for a new access token'. Refresh tokens are single-use: each refresh returns a new one and invalidates the previous access token immediately, so serialize refreshes per user.
steps.title: Run a daily background refresh

steps.detail: Only Public apps can be listed. Follow the App Gallery submission guide and final checklist; expect editorial feedback before publication. Listing is promotion, not a connection prerequisite.
steps.title: (Optional) Submit to the App Gallery

tagline: A public Server/Web app with Auth Code + PKCE; the old sandbox graduation gate was retired in March 2024, so the live review is only for approval-required scopes. Permissions are fixed on the app (the authorize URL's scope parameter is ignored), refresh tokens are opt-in and rotate on a 7-day clock, and Application Type can never be changed.

time.active: ~20 min of console setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day for standard permissions; scope-approval ticket duration not stated
time.waiting: Scope approval (only for 'requires approval' scopes): not stated
